questions.q: Consider a cuboid all of whose edges are integers and whose base is square. Suppose the sum of all its edges is numerically equal to the sum of the areas of all its six faces. Then the sum of all its edges is.
questions.solution:
Let sides are $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{h}\begin{array}{l}
\text { So, } 4 a+4 h+4 a=2\left(a^{2}+a h+a h\right) \\
2 a+2 h+2 a=a^{2}+2 a h \\
\Rightarrow a^{2}-4 a=2 h(1-a) \\
\Rightarrow\left(a^{2}-1\right)+1-4(a-1)-4=2 h(1-a) \\
\Rightarrow(a-1)(a+1)-4(a-1)-3=2 h(1-a) \\
\Rightarrow 2 h=\frac{3}{a-1}+4-(a+1)
\end{array}$
So $a=2 \& h=2$ are the only integral solution (a $\& h$ are positive integers)

questions.q: In a classroom, one-fifth of the boys leave the class and the ratio of the remaining boys to girls is $2: 3$. If further 44 girls leave the class, the ratio of boys to girls is $5: 2$. How many more boys should leave the class so that the number of boys equals that of girls?
questions.solution:
Let no of Boys $=x\&$ Let no of girls $=y$
Given $\frac{\left(\frac{4 x}{5}\right)}{y}=\frac{2}{3}\frac{2 x}{5 y}=\frac{1}{3}y=\frac{6 x}{5}$ .........(i)
Also, $\frac{\left(\frac{4 x}{5}\right)}{y-44}=\frac{5}{2}8 x=25(y-44)8 x=25\left(\frac{6 x}{5}-44\right)$ (use 1)
$x=50y=60$
